course.title: Electronics Foundations
course.description: Learn how simple circuits behave through diagrams, calculations, and experiments.
course.audience: A beginner using an Arduino starter kit or studying introductory electricity.

modules.title: Electric circuits
modules.description: Build a working model of voltage, current, resistance, and closed paths.

concepts.title: Electric charge
concepts.summary: Electric charge is a property of matter that produces electrical interactions.

concepts.title: Closed circuit
concepts.summary: A continuous conducting path allows charge to move around a circuit.

concepts.title: Voltage
concepts.summary: Voltage describes electric potential difference between two points.

concepts.title: Current
concepts.summary: Current measures the rate at which electric charge passes a point.

concepts.title: Resistance
concepts.summary: Resistance describes how strongly a component opposes current.

concepts.title: Ohm's law
concepts.summary: For an ohmic component, current equals voltage divided by resistance.

lessons.title: Current in a single loop
lessons.orientation: Trace the wire from one battery terminal, through the resistor, and back to the other terminal.
lessons.explanation: Current measures how quickly electric charge passes a point in a circuit. In this single loop, the same path carries charge through the resistor and back to the battery. Ohm's law relates current to voltage and resistance: I = V / R. With 5 V and 100 Ω, the current is 0.05 A.

visualBrief.learningPurpose: Show one closed circuit and the direction used to describe conventional current.
facts: The wire forms one closed path.
The battery supplies a potential difference.
The resistor is in series with the battery.
Current has the same value at every point in this ideal single loop.

objects.name: Resistor
objects.description: One resistor placed in the loop.

visualBrief.altTextDraft: A battery and resistor are connected by one closed wire loop. An arrow on the top wire shows conventional current around the loop.
verificationChecks: The voltage, resistance, and calculated current agree with Ohm's law.

activities.title: Change the circuit
activities.instructions: Adjust voltage or resistance. Predict the effect before reading the calculated current.
activities.predictionPrompt: What will happen to current when resistance increases while voltage stays fixed?

questions.prompt: A 5 V battery is connected across a 100 Ω resistor. Calculate the current in amperes.
hints: Write Ohm's law as I = V / R.
Substitute 5 V for V and 100 Ω for R.
Divide 5 by 100. Express the result in amperes.

sources.title: Physics: Electric Current, Resistance, and Ohm's Law
sources.notes: Used for introductory definitions and the relationship expressed by Ohm's law.
